Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

almost adverb

also nearly, virtually, just about, more or less, that’s more like it, all but, pretty well, practically nothing, hardly anyone, practically

classical

Plaut. Bacch. 586: forēs paene exfrēgistī
Hor. S. 1.5.71–72: sēdulus hospes paene macrōs ārsit dum turdōs versat in ignī
Traupman 270

paene

adverb · Wiktionary

almost, nearly

Other words

  • prope — nearly, almost (of degree)

    adverb · also used · classical · Liv. 21.56.6: elephantōs prope omnēs absūmpsit · Wiktionary

  • propemodum — nearly, just about; as an answer, “nearly”

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 211c–211d: Quid sī sīc? — Propemodum.; Cic. Tusc. 1.94: in eādem propemodum brevitāte quā illae bēstiolae reperiēmur; Traupman 101, 102: propemodum; propemodum est, that’s more like it; Traupman 106: pretty well (just about), propemodum; Traupman 335; Traupman 402 · Wiktionary

  • ferē — nearly, almost; with a negative, hardly any

    adverb, after the word it qualifies · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.15: nihil ferē intellegit (Lewis & Short); Cic. Mur. 6: nēmō ferē saltat sōbrius (Lewis & Short, by chapter); Traupman 26: nihil ferē, practically nothing · Wiktionary

    Nihil ferē, practically nothing; nēmō ferē, hardly anyone.

Examples

  • Paene!

    Almost!composed

  • Paene fēcistī!

    You almost did it!composed

  • Satin' sīc est? — Nōn. — Quid sī sīc? — Propemodum. — Quid sī sīc? — Sat est.

    Is this all right? — No. — What about this? — Nearly. — And this? — That’ll do.Ter. Ph. 211–211f

  • forēs paene exfrēgistī. quid nunc vīs tibi?

    you nearly broke the door down. What do you want now?Plaut. Bacch. 586
